summary:
Repair needed (PRE-REGISTERED, measure first; qa ruling 2026-10-18): light-dispatch resolveTask (src/index.ts ~686-700, answerOutcome after f2dfbf3) treats any JSON answer that lacks success:false and is not shape structuredError as a SUCCESS — including answers that say resolved:false (a non-result). The budget case (resolved:false + dispatch_budget_exhausted) is fixed narrowly in f2dfbf3; broadening to every resolved:false was DEFERRED because its blast radius is unmeasured (a template may rely on a 'not found' resolved:false letting the chain continue). Plan: (1) the database fork reads a 24 h read-only count of resolved:false answers per template on one node, and whether each sits on a non_fatal task; (2) state a per-template expectation; (3) mark the legitimate 'not found continues' tasks non_fatal; (4) then treat resolved:false as failure. | 
[2026-10-18 database fork measurement, read-only] NO measurable BEFORE: answer bodies are not persisted (task records hold attempts, budget_ms, duration_ms, impulse ids, resolver_id, resolver_tier, success, task_id, tool_calls; output_impulses = []), and there are 0 resolved:false lines in the dev-vessel, llm-resolver and light-dispatch journals over 24 h. Budget refusals (17/24 h in llm-resolver, 11 from resolver-author) reach light-dispatch as structuredError and already count as failures. So step (1) becomes INSTRUMENT FIRST: stamp the answer's resolved flag on the task record (or count resolved:false per template in ld /health), measure, then decide the classification change.
falsifier_spec: must-fail (after the count): a resolved:false answer on a fatal task fails the task; control: a resolved:false on a non_fatal task lets the chain continue.
